action.title: HOLD at planned level
action.detail: Keep marketing and acquisition budgets at the planned level, but do not step them up: Bitcoin is down about 6% in a week and about 24% in a month, a Rally watch drop window has been open since 11 November, and the headline could turn BEARISH later this week if the weakness lasts. Keep a reserve ready instead of cutting, because the long-run base is still rising; spend now on retention, trust and education, and step up acquisition only once price closes back above the 200-week average ($67,975) and then the 200-day average ($72,236). This is a budget posture, not trading advice.

analysis: Bottom line: Bitcoin is holding just above $61,000 after last week's fall, but fear is extreme and the month still leans down, so today is about calm, safety and steady spending, not promotions. Short term, the picture is weak: Bitcoin has closed under its 50-day average for 33 days in a row, sits about 20% below it and about 25% under its 30-day high, and Fear & Greed reads 11 out of 100. News is nudging the mood a little lower, as two more cross-chain hacks hit Chainflip (losses now about $12 million) and Fusionist, and Asian stocks opened lower again on Monday (PANews). A normal week lately swings about $3,971, so a close above $63,250 (the top of a typical week's swing) would turn the week up, a close below $58,952 (the 30-day low) would turn it down, and in between it stays choppy; safety and explainer messages fit better than offers right now.

The next month leans down: price is about 24% lower than 30 days ago and about 22% lower than 90 days ago, and the medium-term reading has now been in its weak zone for three days in a row; the model needs five before the headline switches from NEUTRAL to BEARISH. On the other side, Abraxas Capital bought about $897 million of Bitcoin into the drop (PANews), while institutions quoted by PANews expect US inflation (October PCE, due this week) to rise to 3.8%, which may raise talk of a Fed rate rise in December. Bitcoin would have to win back $76,173 (the 50-day average) before the month can firm up, and only above $86,603 (the 90-day high) is there real room to climb. The Fed meeting on 8 December is the next big scheduled event; keep bigger campaign pushes until after a clear turn.

The 3-6 month picture still leans up, but only barely: the 200-day average is still rising (about 4.5% over 90 days), yet price is about 15% under it, about 10% under its 200-week average and about 51% below its all-time high. The recovery is only back on track if Bitcoin closes above $72,236 (the 200-day average) again; $67,975 (the 200-week average) is the floor price has slipped under, and $124,753 (the all-time high) stays the far marker. Slow structural steps continue, such as Malaysia's Maybank testing government-bond settlement on blockchain (PANews). More weeks under the 200-week average would turn this picture down and be the time to shift budget toward keeping existing users.
